#1345. Ruben Amorim rips into his AC Milan players after embarrassing Europa League defeat: Ex-Man United boss hits out at team's attitude and criticises 'awful' performance

Published: 16:34 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EDT, 5 November 2026

Ruben Amorim savaged his AC Milan side for their 'awful' attitude and performance in losing to Hungarian minnows Ferencvaros.

The former Man United boss presided over a 2-0 defeat in the Europa League on Thursday night in front of furious home supporters at the San Siro.

To make matters worse, the visitors even played the last 15 minutes with ten men but Milan were still unable to break through.

Amorim, 41, who was sacked from his post at Old Trafford last season and took over the Italian club in the summer, gave a brutal assessment of his team after the loss.

'When you play for Milan, you have a responsibility; you can't go out there like this,' he said at his post-match press conference.

'We're not ready to compete on both fronts in Serie A and Europe; we need to work on our approach to matches.

Ruben Amorim could hardly believe what he was seeing on a dreadful night for AC Milan

The home side suffered an embarrassing defeat by Ferencvaros at the San Siro

'There's nothing I can say tonight; we had to win; it was an important match. I can't say anything to defend the team; we need to understand what happened.'

He went on: 'Maybe I did something wrong in the last few days. Last year, the team had similar problems, and today we weren't ready; we didn't have the attitude to try to come back at all costs when we were behind.

'Tonight, we have no excuses. Whoever was on the pitch could have won this match. We have to resolve these ups and downs; we should have done many things much better, even just on second balls: that alone would have made things go differently.

'The first half, in particular, was awful; it's about ambition, attitude, and concentration. We weren't ready to move from the derby to another competition.'

Amorim's side are fifth in Serie A, seven points off top spot, and struggling massively in Europe down in 28th place – outside of the qualification spots for the knockout stages.

Even though Amorim made changes to the side that beat Inter in the derby at the weekend, he insisted the team should have had enough to beat Ferencvaros.

He went on: 'We're not mentally ready. The technical aspect has nothing to do with it. The rotation has nothing to do with it. You can't tell me that the starting line-up wasn't up to the task of winning the game.

'We gave ourselves all the chances we had, especially at the start. I take full responsibility for this, because the team is my responsibility, but we can't afford to do something like this, especially in the first half, in front of our fans, at our home. We can't do this; we have to improve, otherwise it's over.

'We want to do well in the Europa League too, we need to rotate and win like that too. We're not ready to play every three days now, but I certainly won't give up on the Europa League. We'll fight until it's over. It's a promise.'

Ferencvaros fans in the away end enjoyed one of the most memorable nights in their history

Amorim's results at AC Milan have been mixed after a positive start at his new club. He opted to take charge of the Italian giants having been out of work since his dismissal at United.

The Portuguese's reign at Old Trafford was disastrous. He oversaw the club's lowest Premier League finish (15th) after joining in November 2024.

And he only managed to win 38 per cent of United's games, taking 58 points from 47 games in the Premier League in total.

Amorim will hope the Ferencvaros result is a blip and AC Milan will have the chance to bounce back against Genoa on Sunday.

#1344. Man Utd 'Contacted' Over Deal to Sign Alejandro Balde From Barcelona

Manchester United have learned what they need to do to strengthen at full-back with a move for Alejandro Balde in the January transfer window.

Michael Carrick's tenure in charge at Old Trafford has fallen apart this term off the back of an uneven transfer window that focused heavily on revamping the midfield department and seemingly left the squad lacking elsewhere.

Despite the rousing Champions League comeback victory against Roma in midweek United are still winless in the Premier League since August and are languishing down in 17th place.

The midfield overhaul hasn't had the impact that might have been hoped and a disrupted defensive unit has also played a major part in the dreadful form.

Full-back was an area that many expected to be strengthened in the summer but now, better late than never, the club have the conditions laid out to bring in Spain international Balde to help address the issue.

The 23-year-old's agent, Jorge Mendes, has been busy putting in the groundwork for a move away from the Camp Nou in January, with the Premier League considered the primary destination.

According to Sport in Spain, the Portuguese super agent has been in communication with United, who need help at left-back urgently thanks to the unwelcome return of Luke Shaw's fitness problems, along with an injury to Patrick Dorgu.

Carrick has opted to switch Diogo Dalot over from the right while youngster Harry Amass has barely got a look in, but Balde could now be the answer with a decision on his next move expected to be taken in December ahead of the window opening in the New Year.

There is significant competition for his services, however, as Mendes is said to have also informed Liverpool and Aston Villa of what it will take to do a deal, while Manchester City and Tottenham are interested but would require players to leave first.

Italian giants Juventus and Roma have also spoken to Mendes but are thought likely to struggle with Balde's wage requirements, while Monaco and Benfica are interested.

A Balde loan move in January with a permanent option, potentially becoming an obligation if conditions are met, is seen as the preferred option for the player and his representatives.

Barcelona would prefer a sale worth around €40 million (£33.4m) but may be open to an initial loan as it would free up space on their wage bill, and potentially increase Balde's value ahead of a transfer in the summer.

Ronald Araujo's successful loan switch from the Camp Nou to Anfield this season is seen as a positive example to follow for Balde, who wants more first team football.

As such, it could be necessary for United to be able to promise the Spaniard game time for him to choose Old Trafford, as he and his agent want to find a club committed to him and able to provide the opportunity to regain prominence after falling out of favour at the Catalan giants., even though Hansi Flick has praised him in the past.

Speaking in 2025, the Barca boss said: “He has improved a lot,.

He’s one of the best full-backs, a fantastic player. He has more potential and he wants to learn and to get better every day.

The coast is currently clear for Balde, who has only started once this season in the 2-1 Clasico defeat by Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, but whether Shaw and Dorgu's potential returns from injury could cloud the issue is unclear.

Equally relevant is the uncertainty around Carrick's position. If the Englishman is still in a job but at risk of the sack by the time Mendes and Balde decide on a move next month then it might rule United out on the grounds that any replacement manager has other plans for his lineup.

United face Aston Villa on Sunday ahead of the international break where Carrick's future may be decided.

#1343. Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and said he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

“It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel said: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

But on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a big tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

“We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”

We played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find new words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

[Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone showed he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

He’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

A perfect night for me personally and also for the team. It’s been a tough camp, a long camp with some difficult games so it’s nice to finish it off all together. An extremely proud evening for me.

You saw some fantastic football out there tonight. The way we’re moving, the one-touch stuff, a fantastic ball from Elliot to Morgan and then a first time cross which was as good as it gets. As a striker you’re just waiting for those opportunities.

It started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it quickly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

This is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

Secret to Harry Kane’s England longevity? ‘He strikes the ball better than Ronaldo’

Right foot, goal. Left foot, goal. Edge of the area, goal. Inside the area, goal. Under pressure, goal, Right foot, save. Left foot, goal. That was Harry Kane’s warm-up prior to England’s 7-0 demolition of Croatia and it underlined just why the striker will equal Peter Shilton’s appearance record on Tuesday night.

As demonstrated in Rijeka, Kane’s career has been a non-stop pursuit of excellence that has led him to the very top of the national game. England’s record goalscorer will also become the joint most-capped player with Shilton, when he makes his 125th appearance against the Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday night.

Eberechi Eze is set to start for England in the clash against Czech Republic tonight. The Arsenal forward is poised to come in for Anthony Gordon, who has started in the three matches during the Nations League international break. Trent Alexander-Arnold is also due to play at right-back, with Jarell Quansah moving to centre-back to cover for Ezri Konsa.

Alex Scott has been ruled out through injury, which has upset Bournemouth after he played in the win over Croatia at the weekend. Myles Lewis-Skelly is expected to get a recall to the team after playing against Czech Republic in Prague last week when England won 2-0. Morgan Rogers, who scored against Croatia, is in line to start in place of Bukayo Saka.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of England vs Czech Republic from Wembley in the fourth and mercifully final round of fixtures in this sprawling Nations League international break. Tonight Harry Kane will win his 125th cap and equal Peter Shilton for England appearances.

Shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

England played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

In the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. He will have to find replacements for the injured Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa, however, and Calvert Lewin, who has had seven minutes of action, Rio Ngumoha 19, Morgan Gibbs-White 27 and Jarrad Branthwaite one, may feel they deserve a fairer opportunity to show what they can do in a match.

#1342. Milan’s De Winter snubs Belgium call-up, Van Bommel warns: ‘It comes with consequences’

Koni De Winter has turned down a call-up to the Belgium squad, and coach Mark van Bommel has warned the Milan defender that his decision will have long-term consequences.

According to Calciomercato.com, De Winter is not in Belgium’s squad for this month’s Nations League games against Turkey on 12 November and Italy on 15 November. He did not play a single minute in the four group games so far, against Italy, France and Turkey.

“Koni De Winter is absent because he didn’t feel comfortable in his situation and decided not to come. It’s his choice, I can’t do anything about it,” Van Bommel said.

“I spoke to him and explained the situation, as a coach, a former player and a father. You have to accept it, but it has long-term consequences. He’s 24 and he’s a responsible person.”

De Winter joined Milan from Genoa in the summer of 2025 for around €20m. He made 26 appearances in his first season, scoring once.

Under Ruben Amorim he has become a first-choice centre-back, ahead of the injured Matteo Gabbia. He has made 10 Serie A and four Europa League appearances this season, though he struggled in Thursday’s 2-0 home defeat to Ferencváros.

Milan teammate Diego Moreira has been called up by Belgium.

#1341. Leeds Lining Up Most Exciting Signing Since Raphinha in Pavel Sulc

After a strong start to the season, Leeds United have hit a sticky patch in recent weeks after going five Premier League matches without a win.

Leeds have drawn three of those games, with their two defeats coming against the reigning champions Arsenal, and in-form Bournemouth last time out.

Still, the Yorkshire outfit lie in 12th position in the table and while manager Daniel Farke will have ambitions of breaking into the top half and potentially pushing for a European spot this term, it isn't the worst position to be in at this stage of the campaign.

The Whites' record of eight goals conceded in nine matches is strong when you consider that only Arsenal and Brighton have let in fewer goals than they have, with Liverpool and Manchester City among the teams to have conceded more.

More of a pressing concern though is their attacking output, with a current hit rate of one goal per game.

If Leeds and Farke are serious about progressing, that number needs to increase significantly across the rest of the campaign.

There is certainly an overreliance on Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored a third of those and is drawing Man Utd interest amid talk of a new Leeds United contract, while right wing-back Jayden Bogle is second in the rankings with two to his name.

It's no surprise then, that TEAMtalk claim that the 49ers are considering a new attacking addition as soon as the January transfer window, with summer signing Harry Wilson struggling to get going in a white shirt so far.

The report claims that Leeds hold an interest in Gabriel Sara of Galatasaray, who played in England previously with Norwich City, and Coventry City attacking midfielder Jack Rudoni, but they have another notable target in Lyon's Pavel Sulc.

According to the outlet, Leeds also have an admiration for Czechia international Sulc, although he has recently suffered an injury that will keep him on the sidelines until March.

It means that any move for the 25-year-old would have to wait until the summer rather than January, but you can see why the Yorkshire club are looking into a deal to sign the attacking midfielder.

Leeds have a long-term interest in Sulc, and they were heavily linked with a move to bring him to Elland Road in the summer, just 12 months after he joined the Ligue 1 outfit from Viktoria Plzen.

There are always going to be question marks over whether a player can replicate what he did in a smaller league when he joins a top European league, with Sulc scoring 47 and assisting 31 in 167 outings for the Czech outfit.

However, the attacking midfielder made an immediate impact at Lyon and he will be frustrated that he has now been ruled out for months after a positive first year or so at the club.

Leeds have had some great players over the years, with Raphinha being the standout player in recent years.

The Brazilian always showed he had something special, and his career has now gone to new heights given he is one of Barcelona's best players, and is a genuine contender for the Ballon d'Or.

Leeds look like they are in desperate need of a fresh spark in the final third and, given Sulc's attacking output for Lyon, he can be the man to provide it.

It's unclear how much the Czechia international would cost, but the Ligue 1 outfit would surely want a major profit on the €10m they paid in 2025.

If Sulc moved to Elland Road and replicated the numbers he has been producing for the French team, then he would be their most exciting signing since Raphinha.

Leeds United are interested in signing Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott in January.

Ben White was looking round to see if there was anyone in the Leeds line he recognised from his excellent year’s loan with them but Marcelo Bielsa’s promotion heroes have all moved on now. In fact, with Illan Meslier, there are two at the Gunners and none at Elland Road.

Long international break, we recovered most of our players and have a point to prove after our last game.

[Declan Rice] needed that [break] after everything he’s done over the years. He has looked fresh this week.

Everyone is fit and ready to play but we have a very difficult opponent.

We know that today is one of the toughest tasks in European football. They have been the most consistent side in Europe for years. Especially after a warning shot in the last game, they will be on it today.

But we didn’t win our good start in the lottery we earned it. We travel here in confidence.

Brighton didn’t park the bus. They went for it and pressed Arsenal. You need to do this. You have to go for it. If you sit deep their individual quality is too good. The one thing is to have a plan and a theory but another to execute it.

Last season we faced one of the best sides in the world so we didn’t dwell on [those defeats]. If we are at our best we have a chance to compete for points.

There’s no doubt who the biggest threat to Arsenal’s defence will be today: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has four goals in six games in all competitions this season and is the top scoring Englishman in the league since the start of last season. He’s a player Arsenal once looked at signing, many years ago.

Joe Cole is trying to make a case that Manchester City are not guilty of cheating because financial doping is not the same as taking drugs or match-fixing. A man who won all his medals at Abramovich’s Chelsea says it ‘is not right to class it as cheating’.

This is where punditry is broken. A former player may have an opinion on the subject of finance but it does not sound as though he is particularly informed and yet he’s given time to witter on because he doesn’t ‘feel’ it’s right.

The most interesting aspect of that Arsenal lineup, I think, is the inclusion of Noni Madueke. It seems like he’ll be on the left flank, as the replacement for the injured Christos Tzolis. Madueke has played a handful of games on the left since joining Arsenal from Chelsea but it hasn’t happened nearly as frequently as had been expected when he first arrived. A left-footer on the left wing: old-school!

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#1339. Bologna coach Palladino: ‘I’d like a visit from Kimi Antonelli’

Raffaele Palladino has invited Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli to visit Bologna, and has warned his side to stay level-headed after three straight wins before Saturday’s trip to Parma.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, the Bologna coach opened his pre-match press conference by congratulating the Mercedes driver, a lifelong Rossoblù fan, on becoming the youngest champion in F1 history.

“I wanted to open the press conference by congratulating Kimi Antonelli, because it’s only right. He’s one of Bologna’s excellences, and we’re all happy,” Palladino said. “I’d love for him to come and visit us at the training ground and the stadium. It’s right to congratulate a great champion.”

Bologna have turned their season around since Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco in September. Wins at Cagliari, at Milan (4-2) and at home to Monza have lifted them to 14 points, but the coach insists nobody should get carried away.

“A month ago we weren’t bad, and today we haven’t become phenomenal. We have to be balanced in our judgements,” he said. “We’re growing, and I have good feelings for the future. But defeats and difficult moments will come, and we’ll need to be balanced then too.”

Saturday’s game at the Tardini, which kicks off at 18:00 CET [17:00 GMT], is a return to a club that means a lot to Palladino. He scored Parma’s 1,000th Serie A goal and was in the squad when the club went bankrupt in 2015.

“It was a beautiful and formative experience. We got as far as Europe, then unfortunately there was the bankruptcy, a bad page in Italian football,” he said. “We felt almost abandoned by everyone, and it was sad to see people not getting paid.”

He also warned that Parma, fresh from a 3-0 win at Atalanta, will be dangerous. “They’ve found balance and solidity. The 3-0 in Bergamo says a lot. I expect a test of maturity.”

Artem Dovbyk, Roberto Piccoli and Mikkel Odgaard are all available, while Jay Enem is close to returning. Lorenzo De Silvestri and Emil Holm are still out.

Asked about January, Palladino said: “It’s early for the transfer market, but I believe in this group. When the time comes, I’ll speak to the club, as is right. I came here to build a long-term project.”

#1338. England Duo Elliot Anderson and Djed Spence Have Celebrity Siblings

At every World Cup, a few new England players enter the wider public consciousness. Premier League fans would have been aware of Elliot Anderson and Djed Spence for a little while now, but those who don't follow the sport as closely will probably not know a lot about them.

The pair were trusted by Thomas Tuchel as part of his plans for the 2026 tournament, and were heavily involved throughout. Anderson started every match up until the semi-final defeat against Argentina, later coming off the bench as the Three Lions secured third place against France. Spence also featured in every game, and started in the final two matches against Argentina and Les Bleus as he became a cult hero among fans.

Even some of the most knowledgeable football fans, however, may not know that they both have famous siblings.

Musicians, actors, and other sports stars fill a complete list detailing every 92 club's msot famous supporters.

Whitley Bay-born Anderson came through at Newcastle United but joined Nottingham Forest in 2024. The Magpies will be regretting that as he's since proved to be a top talent, securing a £116m move to Manchester City.

His maternal grandfather, Geoff Allen, actually played for Newcastle United from 1964 to 1968, but it's his brother who will be known to fans of British reality TV. Indeed, his brother, Wil Anderson, became a public figure after appearing on the 11th season of Love Island.

Older brother Wil was actually seen in the US this summer with his fiancée Uma Jammeh, having met her on Love Island in 2024. He is also a boxer and notably took on Britain’s Got Talent legend Jordan Banjo in a Misfits boxing bout, losing via a fourth-round technical knockout in May 2025.

Spence currently plays for Inter Milan, having signed this summer. During the World Cup, he was still a Tottenham player, joining the club in 2022 from Middlesbrough after an impressive loan spell at Nottingham Forest. While it took him a while to earn his place at Spurs (going out on loan three times), the 26-year-old impressed enough in 2025/26 to win a spot in Tuchel's England squad.

His older sister is Karla-Simone Spence, and she is known to the public for being a British actress and voiceover artist. The 29-year-old is most widely recognised for her roles in Blue Story and the ITVX period drama The Confessions of Frannie Langton.

As well as that, Spence's sister has also featured in the BBC series Gold Digger and Wannabe, and she played Haydee in The Count of Monte Cristo alongside well-known actor Sam Claflin.

While Spence will feel as though he did more than enough to make the England World Cup squad, not everybody was convinced. Former England defender John Terry expressed his concerns over the player, telling Piers Morgan:

"Listen, I’m not his fan. I don’t think he’s a good defender, I don’t think he’s a good footballer. He’s played in a really struggling Spurs side this year."

By the time England were knocked out at the semis, though, Spence had won many of his doubters over. He even picked up an assist against France in the third-place play-off. He then earned a big-money move to Inter later that summer.

#1337. Cole Palmer's England lifeline: Three Lions ask Chelsea about star's fitness in clear sign Thomas Tuchel is considering calling him up after warning over last squad withdrawal

Published: 18:32 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 19:13 EDT, 5 November 2026

England have privately asked Chelsea for the latest on Cole Palmer ahead of Thomas Tuchel revealing his squad for the Nations League clashes with Croatia and Spain.

Palmer is under consideration for another call-up, having withdrawn from duty during the last international break with a minor muscular injury.

Tuchel responded by appearing to question his desire to represent his country, warning he 'misses way too many camps' as the 24-year-old skipped all four England fixtures in September and October.

Palmer had played a full 90 for Chelsea away at Bournemouth before that break, which he then used to fly abroad to the Caribbean with his girlfriend, Olivia Holder, after withdrawing from England duty. He was accompanied by a personal rehab coach on that trip, and was provided with an injury-specific training and recovery plan by his club.

Palmer started in Chelsea's first fixture when the Premier League returned at home to Brentford with Blues boss Xabi Alonso insisting they were right to take care of their star player themselves.

Chelsea star Cole Palmer is under consideration for England UEFA Nations League call-up

He withdrew from the last squad, leaving boss Thomas Tuchel questioning his commitment

Palmer, who was injured, went to the Caribbean with girlfriend Olivia Holder on the last international break

It has been described as standard procedure for England to make medical checks on players with clubs. While it does not guarantee a call-up, it indicates how Tuchel has been weighing up offering Palmer another chance as he names his next squad on Friday morning.

Palmer was not the only player to withdraw from England duty in the last break, with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento among other dropouts.

Yet Palmer's issue was a contentious topic after it represented a chance for him to return to England's thinking following his 2026 World Cup omission. His representative did not answer when asked whether he would happily accept another call-up after Tuchel's previous comments.

Palmer has played an important role for Chelsea early in this season with three goals and three assists in the Premier League.

He scored a penalty in their last win over Manchester United, which took him to 50 goals in 105 games in the top flight for the Blues. He has started every league game under Alonso this term with Sunderland at the Stadium of Light this Sunday.

#1336. Liverpool Defeat Adds Weight To Transfer Chase Of Star Tormentor

Liverpool's dramatic defeat to Fenerbahce in midweek looks to have convinced the club to get their own back in the transfer market.

Andoni Iraola's men twice went ahead in Istanbul on Wednesday night but were ultimately beaten 3-2 to end their perfect Champions League record this season.

Goals from Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown cancelled out Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak's, before a winner from Vedat Meriqi took the points.

Brown had a superb game at left-back for the Turkish giants, who were overseen temporarily by ex-Reds forward Dirk Kurt, and he is now reported to be firmly in the sights of the Anfield club as they look to strengthen that position for themselves.

For so long, how to approach the left-back spot at Liverpool was barely a question as Andy Robertson was the unquestioned first choice and, for the most part, consistently available.

But now the Scotland captain is a Tottenham player after his contract expired in the summer and the transition to ex-Bournemouth star Milos Kerkez hasn't gone as smoothly as hoped.

Long-term backup Kostas Tsimikas looks set to depart when his own deal runs out at the end of the campaign and the club are currently making plans to address the situation.

The Greek veteran spent last season on loan at Roma but since Iraola replaced Arne Slot in the summer he has largely chosen him over Kerkez as the preferred option in Europe.

TEAMtalk now report that there is interest in 24-year-old Brown, and after his star turn in midweek helped consign Liverpool to defeat they are tipped to respond by stepping up their pursuit.

As well as his goal, the former Derby County youngster also assisted the winner on Wednesday night and was otherwise dynamic down the left flank.

He is believed to want to test himself with a return to English football at some point in his career, having departed for Europe while he was still a teenager.

Brown's career has taken him to Swiss side Lausanne, Belgium's Gent, and now the Turkish Super Lig since leaving the UK, but there is reportedly widespread interest in bringing him back to England.

While Liverpool have been monitoring Brown as the potential answer to their left-back conundrum they appear to be far from alone, with AC Milan enquiring over a move last summer.

Premier League competition is strong, consisting of long-time Reds rivals Chelsea and Manchester United, while Newcastle, Merseyside neighbours Everton, and Brighton are said to all be monitoring the situation.

Brown, a former England Under-20 international, moved to Turkey from Gent at the start of last season and has made 54 appearances for the club, scoring eight goals and registering nine assists.

#1335. An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Developing artificial intelligence (AI)-native experimental laboratories for autonomous scientific exploration with minimal human intervention represents a long-standing goal. Although autonomous experimental systems are emerging1,2,3,4, especially in chemical and materials science, they remain largely confined to domains with singular objectives, well-defined workflows and simple instrumentation. This limitation may reflect an ‘add-on’ architecture that uses AI as a task-specific tool rather than providing it with a global understanding of experiments, especially under engineering-oriented circumstances. Here we present AutoDNA, an AI-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments. Through the co-design of models, experiments and instruments, AutoDNA realizes the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework. The system autonomously orchestrates over 20 types of instruments across more than 11,000 steps to execute core nucleic acid operations including synthesis, transcription, amplification and sequencing, while human intervention is limited to hardware maintenance tasks, such as reagent and labware replenishment. Across four representative applications, AutoDNA matched expert-optimized enzymatic DNA synthesis yields, accelerated concurrent protocol execution by 3.2-fold, completed an end-to-end DNA data storage cycle with exact recovery of the original digital content, and identified and validated a clinically detected KRAS G13D mutation. AutoDNA establishes a blueprint towards science-as-a-service, accelerating biological discovery and advancing various applications in synthetic biology and information storage.

#1334. Cannavaro: ‘It’s my dream to coach Italy; national team coaching is like a Neapolitan coffee’

Fabio Cannavaro has admitted his dream is to coach the Italian national team, and he still doesn’t understand why Udinese chose not to keep him in 2024.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, the World Cup-winning captain spoke on Sky Sport Italia’s Calcio Unplugged. He is currently in charge of Uzbekistan, whom he led at their first-ever World Cup this summer.

“My goal and my dream, which is normal, is to coach in Italy and to coach the national team,” Cannavaro said. “I’m working for that, not to travel the world and go to Asia. I want to work hard to achieve important objectives.”

Cannavaro’s only Serie A job so far came at Udinese, where he was appointed with five games left of the 2023-24 season and kept the club up on the final day. He was not kept on.

“I had a taste of Serie A in five games, saving Udinese. 99% of the time they keep you on. With me, a different choice was made, and I accepted it,” he said. “It wasn’t explained to me, but I saw it as an experience I was given at a fantastic club, where a coach has everything he needs to improve and do well.”

His comments come days after Udinese sacked Kosta Runjaic and appointed Paolo Zanetti.

The 53-year-old has also coached Al-Nassr, Guangzhou Evergrande and the China national team. “I would make these choices again, because today I have an international background that has helped me grow as a person and as a coach.”

His future in Uzbekistan is uncertain after the postponement of the Asian Cup. “I’ve already met the president. I’m definitely enjoying the experience here a lot, but at the same time I want to coach,” he said. “It’s a country that’s investing a huge amount in youth academies. At the last camp I gave a debut to a 17-year-old.”

Cannavaro also explained what he misses about club football. “The day-to-day for a coach is different. It’s what gives you adrenaline every day: you see the player every day, you talk to him, you try to help him grow and improve, and to prepare for games,” he said.

“Working as a national team coach is like a Neapolitan coffee. It’s short, you have 10 days in which you can’t make a mistake, and you have to find a solution. It’s very stimulating.”

#1333. Miguel Delaney: Man Utd Keen on Replacing Carrick With Sebastian Hoeness

Manchester United's dramatic victory in midweek has given Michael Carrick a stay of execution but new details have emerged on his potential replacement.

The embattled Red Devils came back from two down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday, ending a dreadful run of form which had seen them go without a win in any competition since defeating Sabah almost a month ago.

While the result has lifted the mood around Carrick and his squad, it remains only the first win in 10, and the Premier League picture remains dire.

United are 17th in the table ahead of the visit of Aston Villa on Sunday and haven't beaten anybody in the top flight since Ipswich at the end of August.

If that remains the club's only league win heading into the next international break the possibility that Carrick loses his job remains very real, although a lack of conviction over what to do about his future appears to be prolonging the situation.

Despite long-term links to former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe, the Englishman reportedly doesn't convince the powers that be at Old Trafford as much as widely believed, according to the Independent's Miguel Delaney.

Nobody within the hierarchy in Manchester is apparently prepared to make a decision on how to proceed with the manager position, amid confusion over who should be the proper replacement.

In that context, Sebastian Hoeness at Stuttgart has emerged as an option with some backing, with the German reported to be "highly rated" at Old Trafford.

However, tempering that positive view is the disastrous reign of Carrick's predecessor as permanent manager, Ruben Amorim, whose time in charge of United began almost exactly two years ago but ended in ignominy last January after 14 months in charge.

The Portuguese, now managing AC Milan, arrived from Sporting as a two-time league winner in his home country and with a reputation as one of the best young managers in Europe.

But, having been pushed to join mid-season after the dismissal of Erik ten Hag, he was never able to adapt his methods to the Premier League and spent the rest of the campaign flirting with relegation, before losing the Europa League final to fellow league strugglers Tottenham.

Hoeness took over at Stuttgart with the club bottom of the Bundesliga in 2023 and transformed their fortunes. After avoiding relegation he finished second in his first full season, returning the club to the Champions League after well over a decade, and has reached two DFB Pokal finals since, winning one.

As such, he currently has a similar reputation as Amorim enjoyed prior to his nightmare in England, but it is seen as a similarly "huge" leap from Stuttgart to Manchester United.

Like Amorim, he has favoured a 3-4-3 system in recent weeks, which is very similar to Amorim, although he has also used a 4-2-3-1 formation on plenty of occasions too.

The lack of forward planning among the club's decision makers has compounded issues for successive managers and the current indecision potentially risks doing more of the same.

Backing Ten Hag despite concerns over his long-term suitability blew up in United's face, leading them to pressure Amorim to take over a squad built in his predecessor's image without a summer to implement his ideas.

The Portuguese never recovered and when Carrick led an Ole Gunnar Solskjaer-style revival last term, he was rewarded with the permanent job just like the Norwegian, only for things to fall apart this season.

Unless the Roma victory is the start of an unlikely rise from the ashes of this campaign, then the next manager, whoever it may be, faces an ever-growing task of turning the club around.

#1332. 'Winning at the Emirates is very hard... but we were a team of warriors': Hull City hero GEOVANNI on his iconic goal against Arsenal, why it very nearly never happened and why the Tigers 'will always be in my heart'

Published: 21:00 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EDT, 5 November 2026

The greatest moment in Hull City's Premier League history began with Geovanni trying to go home.

'I was ill all night, I barely slept at all,' says Geovanni, who was gripped by a fever and thumping headache less than 24 hours before he was due to walk out at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in September 2008. The Brazilian rang his wife from the team hotel to tell her he was coming home and planned to have someone pick him up.

Thankfully, his wife Roberta would not hear of it.

'God really used her that day,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'She said: "Geovanni, stay there, God will honour you. Hang on and tomorrow try to get a bit of sleep."'

When Hull staff came to his room the next morning, he asked to be left to sleep. He dosed up on medicine and went for lunch, but sat out the light pre-match training session with his temperature touching 38 degrees Celsius.

'And then I got to that game, which was so spectacular,' he says, 'and I was able to score and help Hull beat Arsenal.'

Geovanni unleashes a spectacular equaliser for Hull at the Emirates Stadium back in September 2008

The goal inspired a famous comeback win for the Tigers, who became only the second team to win away at Arsenal

It was Hull's first league meeting with Arsenal for 93 years, in the first top-flight season of the club's then 104-year history.

Arsene Wenger's side had started the day top of the table and Paul McShane's own goal put Arsenal ahead after 51 minutes. Most expected the floodgates to open.

But 11 minutes later up stepped Hull's brilliant Brazilian, a marquee signing from Manchester City in the summer of 2008 after the Tigers' unexpected promotion.

Geovanni cut inside Theo Walcott and sent a 25-yard rocket into Manuel Almunia's top corner. Daniel Cousin headed in a historic winner four minutes later and Hull became only the second side to beat Arsenal at the Emirates.

'Beating Arsenal at the Emirates is very hard, and we pulled it off,' says Geovanni, now 46, speaking from his home in Brazil. 'That was a team of warriors, great players, and we had a really good friendship. And that day we walked away with a great win.'

On Saturday, Hull return to the Emirates to face the champions and league leaders. The Tigers are 11th after nine games. It is a strong start that few predicted.

'Hull have to give 100 per cent, the maximum, be switched on the whole time,' says Geovanni. 'It's difficult, but it's not impossible, because Hull really did beat Arsenal.'

Eight days after the Emirates match, Geovanni did it again. A stunning 30-yard free-kick at White Hart Lane nestled into the top corner past his friend and compatriot Heurelho Gomes.

'We beat Tottenham with Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, all those players,' he says. 'For me, those two are top-drawer. They're two great players who left a mark on me.'

The win moved Hull into third and by the end of October they were level on points at the top. 'London 0 Hull 2' read the headline in the local paper, in reference to Hull band The Housemartins' 1986 album London 0 Hull 4, as the city revelled in its newfound fame.

Geovanni (centre) was part of another iconic Premier League moment, when Phil Brown gave his team a public dressing down at half-time of a loss at Manchester City

The Brazilian returned to Hull's MKM Stadium last year and received a hero's welcome

Geovanni took centre stage. Arriving on a free that summer after being released by Manchester City, he credits manager Phil Brown and assistant Brian Horton for giving him a second chance in the Premier League.

'They were very special people in allowing me to stay in England, which was my dream,' he says. 'And I learned a lot from both of them. Brian was a very experienced coach, he played for Hull, he managed there, so the affection and respect are huge. Whenever I can talk about them, I do.

'In the first year, Hull surprised a lot of people precisely because of the way we played. Sometimes we'd start in a 4-3-1-2, I played as the No10 behind two strikers. And if we were struggling to mark, I'd drop in to close down the left flank and we'd go back to a 4-4-2.'

The dressing room did the rest. Richard Garcia, an Australian winger with Uruguayan parents, helped translate team talks from English into Spanish and captain Ian Ashbee, Nicky Barmby and Bernard Mendy all made Geovanni feel welcome. 'I'm really happy about the friendships I made in that dressing room,' he says.

Geovanni was part of another of the Premier League's most iconic moments, when he and his team-mates received a public dressing down from his manager on the pitch at half-time of a 5-1 loss to Manchester City on Boxing Day 2008. Eleven months later, Jimmy Bullard scored a penalty before recreating the telling off in celebration.

'It was good for breaking the ice,' says Geovanni. 'From that day on the atmosphere got better too, because we can all make mistakes. The most important thing is to admit the mistake and move on.'

Geovanni's finest moment for Manchester City, with whom he spent one season after stints with Barcelona, Benfica and Cruzeiro, came in the Manchester derby, where he was called into the side by manager Sven-Goran Eriksson because Stephen Ireland was ill.

'He called me over and said, "Geovanni, this game... are you ready?". That was the best news I'd had all day, knowing I was going to start.' The day did, in fact, get better. Geovanni scored the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

Geovanni smashes home a winner for City in the Manchester derby, a year before his move to Hull

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages

He struck again against United in November 2008, in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages, while he also scored in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford in 2008.

'A player has to turn up in the big games,' he says. 'United were a machine back then: Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville, Anderson, Ronaldo, Rooney.'

Geovanni's greatest regret, though, remains that he didn't heed the advice of Barca boss Louis van Gaal, who wanted to turn the wannabe striker into a wing-back.

He reflects: 'If I could go back in time, I'd listen to what Van Gaal said, because it would have been easier for me to fight for a place at wing-back than as a striker, where there were great players: Javier Saviola, Rivaldo, Patrick Kluivert, Marc Overmars.'

Luiz Felipe Scolari, his coach at Cruzeiro, gave him his only senior Brazil cap, against Mexico at the 2001 Copa America. 'It was a dream for me: to leave a town of 4,000 people (Acaiaca) and one day represent Brazil,' he says. 'He (Scolari) was a father to me.'

These days Geovanni is a volunteer pastor in Belo Horizonte and runs a players' agency with his father-in-law and an old youth-team friend.

But Hull will always be in his heart. He has a picture of himself in a Hull shirt in his house and received a hero's return after heading back to the city last year.

'I love them (the fans). I have a very special affection for the Hull supporters,' he says. 'It was two years in which I gave everything. I went back there last year and was really well received, it was great: friends from my time there, the fans too.

Battling Blackburn's Damien Duff in a pre-season friendly in his Barcelona days. He spent only two seasons with the Catalan club, having left Cruzeiro to move to Europe

'I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart'

'And I know I left my mark on the club's history. Whenever people talk about Hull City, about Brazilians, they'll remember Geovanni, the time I spent there, the feats we achieved together.

'And I believe I gave those fans a lot of joy, in games that seemed impossible. God blessed me and I was able to score goals and bring joy to that city. I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart.

'My two years at Hull were perhaps the two most special years for me. The sweetest spell of my career.'

#1331. Robert Pires Named the ‘Toughest Opponent’ He’s Ever Played Against

Former Arsenal and France winger Robert Pires did not need a second to think when asked who the toughest opponent of his career was, before picking an iconic English defender.

Of course, based off that description, one would usually assume he was on about either Rio Ferdinand - whom he had many battles with during the Gunners' intense Premier League title rivalry with Manchester United in the mid-2000s - or legendary Chelsea captain John Terry.

But having played against so many defenders during his illustrious career, it was another Three Lions star that got his flowers off of Pires, who would get the better of his marker more often than not, to rack up 180 goals and 119 assists during his playing days, where he won two league titles under Arsene Wenger alongside a World Cup for France.

Alongside Terry and Ferdinand - both named among the top three greatest centre-backs in Premier League history - Pires also snubbed the likes of Jaap Stam, Marcel Desailly, and Ashley Cole.

Instead, when faced with the question about his toughest opponent, he explained to Sky Sports that Gary Neville would usually get the better of their duels. He said:

"He kicked me all game! Old Trafford, Highbury, he was always shouting. It was normal because of the rivalry between Arsenal and Manchester United."

A wind-up merchant of the highest order, it would seem that the now-pundit's tactics of goading his opponents worked on some players, including Pires, and that's what made Neville stand out, even beyond his own defensive brilliance.

One of Jamie Carragher's funniest quotes is when he once remarked 'nobody wants to grow up to be a Gary Neville.' But as the modern full-back role evolves from its defensive foundations, and Pires gave his former Red Devils' adversary some well-deserved praise, it's easy to forget just how good Sir Alex Ferguson's right-back was during a period of unprecedented success.

These two had plenty of memorable battles.

Better known more as a pundit these days - and one of the highest-paid at that - Neville made 602 appearances for United, winning two Champions League titles and an incredible 10 Premier League crowns, all while tirelessly running up and down the right flank.

His era came during a time when the traditional winger - like Pires - was thriving, not afraid to run at the defence and make a direct attacking impact. It was by no means an easy time to defend in English football, but a time that Neville grabbed by the scruff of the neck.

Keinan Davis is a late doubt with a muscle problem, and Vakoun Bayo has only just returned from a hamstring injury. #1329. Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”

#1328. He Was Spurs’ Record Transfer - Now He’s 29, Without A Club, and Worth Just £1.6m

Just seven years after becoming Tottenham Hotspur's record signing, Tanguy Ndombele finds himself without a club.

Born in Longjumeau near Paris, Ndombele rose through the ranks at Guingamp and Amiens, before signing for Lyon in 2017. After enjoying two exceptional years with Les Gones, Tottenham forked out a fee worth upwards of £64 million to bring the midfielder to North London.

He went on to make just 91 appearances for the Lilywhites, before a series of uninspiring loan spells resulted in his contract with Spurs being mutually terminated.

Signing a two-year contract at Nice following his departure from the Premier League in 2024, he failed to impress in the South of France and has subsequently been unemployed since being released in the summer.

Having made his debut in Ligue 2 for Amiens at the age of 18, Ndombele was revered as one of the up-and-coming French talents to watch out for. It wasn't long before Lyon came calling, and he was shining on the biggest stage in his home country.

After making 96 appearances for the Ligue 1 giants and helping them reach the Champions League knockout stages in 2018/19, Ndombele attracted interest from several of Europe's biggest clubs in the 2019 summer transfer window. Tottenham reportedly fended off competition from the likes of Real Madrid and Juventus to secure the signature of the then 22-year-old, who was also beginning to establish himself in the French national team under Didier Deschamps.

The North Londoners, who had just reached a Champions League final, paid a premium for the number eight. The £64 million fee surpassed their previous club record signing, Davinson Sanchez, who had joined from Ajax two years earlier for around £38 million.

This substantial outlay came with hefty expectations, and the pressure this created clearly got to the player. Towards the end of his debut campaign in English football, Spurs boss Jose Mourinho publicly criticised Ndombele for what the manager believed to be a lack of professionalism.

"He's a player with great talent," Mourinho told BBC Sport in 2020.

"He has to know he has to do much better and know I cannot keep giving him opportunities to play because the team is much more important."

This unprofessional tag stuck to Ndombele, with the next few Spurs managers not taking a liking to him either. Ryan Mason, Nuno Espirito Santo and Antonio Conte all granted the player few opportunities to impress (barring a relatively promising 2020/21 season), while persistent fitness issues derailed his time in N17.

He was eventually loaned back to Lyon in an attempt to revitalise his career. After this stint failed, he spent a season each at Napoli and Galatasaray before Tottenham and his representatives agreed to terminate his agreement with the North London club in 2024.

Walking into the job market as a damaged asset, desperately in need of a permanent home, Nice offered him a lifeline back in France in the summer of 2024. Ndombele took this opportunity, signing a two-year deal with the Ligue 1 club.

Despite impressing in his first season under Franck Haise at the Allianz Riviera, the box-to-box midfielder struggled in his second campaign, making just 13 appearances across all competitions. This disappointing second year cost him a new contract, meaning he once again entered the market as a free agent.

He's yet to be offered a lifeline this time around, and TransferMarkt subsequently values the ex-Spurs man at just €2 million (£1.67 million).

The wages of every player at Tottenham for the 2026/27 season, including that of James Maddison and Dominic Solanke.

According to the Sun, Ndombele went on trial at Russian club Rubin Kazan back in October. The Russian Premier League outfit seemingly gave the Frenchman an opportunity to prove that he's still at the level, but there have been no reports that he's been offered a contract since.

The 29-year-old remains available, but the longer he goes without finding a new club, the more difficult it becomes to envisage him returning to the pitch professionally.

#1327. ‘Nico Paz is 100% a Como player’ – Ludi addresses future amid Real Madrid, Chelsea and Manchester United links

Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi insists Nico Paz is “100% a Como player”, but admits Real Madrid still have the right to take him back.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, Ludi was speaking to Radio Radio and addressed speculation over the Argentine’s future. Paz has been one of the stars of the Champions League this season, with three goals and five assists in four games. Those include two goals and an assist in Como’s 4-1 win over Manchester United.

His form has attracted interest from Chelsea, Manchester United and Arsenal. Real Madrid could bring him back in 2027.

“I put myself in the shoes of Como fans, because every November and every March, I don’t know whether it’s media speculation or for other reasons, it always comes out that Real Madrid are taking all the players back home,” Ludi said. “This year they’re talking about Jacobo Ramón, and over the next two seasons about Nico Paz.”

Real activated a buy-back clause on Paz in the summer, but Como then re-signed him permanently for a reported €60m. As part of that deal, Real kept another buy-back option, reportedly worth €80m and valid only in summer 2027.

“The truth is that we did a good deal last summer. Nico Paz is 100% a Como player,” Ludi explained. “Real Madrid kept a right to buy him back by a certain date, within the transfer window, as is normal.

“It would still be a sale that would reward our work and would also be important for the club. We’ll work out how to manage the situation during the season, as we’ve always done in recent years, thanks in part to the fantastic relationship we have with Madrid. For now, we have to enjoy the player, because he really is an incredible talent.”

#1326. Page Stunner Helps Leicester City Avoid FA Cup Upset Against Oxford City

A clinical second 45 minutes cancelled out two first-half wonder goals, and ultimately helped 2021’s FA Cup winners Leicester City to avoid a shock exit from this year's competition at the first hurdle.

Louis Page’s stunner broke the deadlock; however, Oxford City’s Scott Pollock came up with his own moment of magic to level up proceedings, scoring direct from a corner.

In the second half, the goals kept coming, though Leicester’s quality proved too much for a defiant Oxford side.

The game got off to a fairly tepid start, with Page’s stunning effort after 16 minutes proving to be the catalyst for the game springing into life.

The teenager found the ball way outside the area, but opted to take aim, and rightly so, as his effort nestled into the top left corner.

Oxford soon responded with chances of their own. Ellis Brown was a major threat on the right-hand side, winning plenty of corners. In the 31st minute, one of them proved crucial. Boyhood Leicester fan Scott Pollock whipped the ball into the area and the delicious cross evaded the clusters of men in the area and ultimately sailed into the far corner. Franco Ravizolli was in no man’s land; Pollock was in dreamland.

Between the equaliser and half-time, Leicester looked to take the sting out of the game. They slowed down proceedings, whilst also attempting to quieten down the partisan atmosphere.

After the break, Russell Martin opted for an offensive change with winger Harry Howell replacing Caleb Okoli. It was a move that was soon vindicated. By the 53rd minute, the Brighton loanee got to the byline, before delivering a ball which was wonderfully met by Emil Riis, who headed it home.

Six minutes later, Leicester had a third. Kamari Doyle’s outside-the-foot finish beat Jonny Maxted, giving the Foxes a much-needed two-goal cushion.

However, just after the hour mark, Oxford showed they weren’t going down without a fight. Captain Josh Ashby was found in behind, and from there he found the back of the net.

Ultimately, the comeback was short-lived, though. With 10 minutes of normal time to go, Tommy Watson found a fourth. The winger's footwork proved too tricky, and despite the angle, he managed to poke the ball into the far corner.

That ensured Leicester made it through to the second round of the cup, but it didn’t come easy. The likes of Howell and Watson changed the game, helping overcome a tough Oxford side.

The FA Cup can offer life-changing prize funds for teams lower down the football pyramid.
